K.question: What evidence is most relevant to polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials for antigen, protein, vaccine, mRNA, or biomacromolecule delivery?
K.summary: This study developed a ternary lipopolyplex (LPP) platform using hyperbranched poly-L-lysine (HBPL) for mRNA delivery, demonstrating high transfection efficiency, enhanced dendritic cell maturation, efficient in vivo delivery to lungs and spleen, and sustained protein expression after one month of storage, highlighting the potential of HBPL-based LPPs for mRNA therapeutics and vaccines.
reported_outcomes: transfection efficiency across multiple cell lines
in vivo mRNA delivery to lungs and spleen
reported_qualitative_findings: HBPL enabled a unique balance between high mRNA encapsulation efficiency, efficient intracellular release, and exceptional colloidal stability
Platform had higher transfection efficiency compared to linear ε-PLL-based counterpart
Enhanced dendritic cell maturation
Superior biocompatibility over a commercial transfection reagent
Efficient mRNA delivery to lungs and spleen with sustained protein expression after 1 month of storage
K.material_or_molecular_context: Hyperbranched poly-L-lysine (HBPL) as part of a ternary lipopolyplex (LPP) with lipid and mRNA
K.biological_context: Multiple cell lines (in vitro), dendritic cells (in vitro and ex vivo), and mouse model (in vivo: lungs and spleen)
limitations: Only tested for mRNA delivery, not directly for other biomacromolecules (e.g., proteins, antigens, or vaccines)
No explicit comparison to other polylysine variants beyond linear ε-PLL
Abstract does not report quantitative numeric results (e.g., transfection percentages or expression levels)
In vivo data limited to lung and spleen expression; no immune response or vaccine efficacy data
K.title: Hyperbranched Polylysine-Based Lipopolyplexes Enable Efficient mRNA Delivery With Long-Term Storage Stability.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials for antigen, protein, vaccine, mRNA, or biomacromolecule delivery?
K.summary: L15K6, a polyleucine-polylysine nano adjuvant, enhances antigen uptake, dendritic cell maturation, and TLR4 signaling, inducing strong antibody responses against GAS and model antigens, outperforming alum.
reported_outcomes: antigen-specific IgG response with antibacterial activity
immune responses against ovalbumin and bovine serum albumin
reported_qualitative_findings: markedly enhances antigen uptake by dendritic cells
promotes antigen-presenting cell maturation
upregulates Toll-like receptor expression, particularly TLR4
robust NF-κB pathway activation
induces robust antigen-specific IgG with potent antibacterial activity
enhances immune responses against model antigens
a single immunization outperforms alum adjuvant in eliciting BSA-specific IgG
K.material_or_molecular_context: L15K6: 15-mer polyleucine coupled with a polylysine unit (K6)
K.biological_context: dendritic cells; Group A Streptococcus (clinical strains); ovalbumin and bovine serum albumin as model antigens; in vitro antibacterial activity; in vivo single immunization
limitations: The study focuses on protein/peptide antigens, not mRNA or other biomacromolecules

K.title: Development of a Novel Polyleucine-Based Immunopotentiator for Subunit Vaccines Against Group A Streptococcus.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials for antigen, protein, vaccine, mRNA, or biomacromolecule delivery?
K.summary: This study reports a cationic polypeptide micelle system based on PEG-PLL-PLLeu (containing poly(L-lysine) block) for antigen delivery. It encapsulates OVA with high loading capacity and significantly enhances antibody production by 70-90 fold, promotes dendritic cell maturation, antigen uptake/presentation, and germinal center formation. Co-delivery with TLR3 agonist PIC also augments CTL response.
reported_qualitative_findings: Polypeptide micelles spontaneously encapsulated OVA antigens with great stability
Enhanced vaccine-induced antibody production
Co-delivery of OVA and PIC synergistically augmented CTL response
Polypeptide micelles could be a robust adjuvant to enhance vaccine-induced immune responses
K.biological_context: In vitro dendritic cell assays and in vivo murine model (implied by vaccine studies)
limitations: Uses OVA as model antigen, not mRNA or other biomacromolecules directly
Co-formulated with TLR3 agonist PIC; not tested as standalone delivery for mRNA or protein vaccines
No direct evidence for polylysine-only materials; study uses block copolymer with PEG and leucine blocks
K.title: Cationic polypeptide micelle-based antigen delivery system: a simple and robust adjuvant to improve vaccine efficacy.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to intracellular uptake, internalization, or endosomal behavior of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: This study compared poly(L-lysine) (PK) and poly(L-arginine) (PR) polyplexes to identify the rate-limiting step in gene transfection. By using microinjection to bypass natural uptake, they quantified intranuclear transcription efficiency and endosomal escape. They found that endosomal escape is the rate-limiting step, independent of the buffering effect, and that transcription efficiency is similar for PK and PR but decreases with molecular weight.
reported_qualitative_findings: intranuclear transcription efficiency is the same in PR and PK and decreases rapidly with increasing molecular weight
transcription efficiency strongly suppressed at high molecular weight
rate-limiting step is buffering effect-independent endosomal escape
cellular uptake and in vitro transfection with or without chloroquine were considered
K.material_or_molecular_context: poly(L-lysine) (PK) and poly(L-arginine) (PR) with different molecular weights
K.biological_context: living cells (microinjection technique applied to cultured cells, cell type not specified)
limitations: microinjection technique bypasses natural endocytic uptake and internalization pathways
focus is on polyplexed pDNA, not free polylysine or lysine-based materials
cell type not specified, limiting generalizability
direct comparison with polyarginine may obscure behavior specific to polylysine alone
K.title: Quantitative comparison between poly(L-arginine) and poly(L-lysine) at each step of polyplex-based gene transfection using a microinjection technique.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to intracellular uptake, internalization, or endosomal behavior of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: Poly-L-lysine dendrimers (G3) are internalized via multiple endocytosis pathways (cholesterol-, dynamin-mediated, macropinocytosis) and trafficked to endosomes and lysosomes in Caco-2 cells; the site of fluorophore conjugation affects uptake and subcellular localization.
reported_outcomes: elucidate endocytosis mechanisms and subcellular localization
impact of fluorophore conjugation on cytotoxicity, uptake, and transepithelial transport
reported_qualitative_findings: Uptake highly dependent on cholesterol- and dynamin-mediated endocytosis and macropinocytosis
Dendrimers were trafficked to endosomes and lysosomes
Subcellular localization impacted by fluorophore conjugation site
Internalization and trafficking can be impacted by conjugation
K.material_or_molecular_context: Poly-L-lysine (PLL) G3 dendrimers conjugated with Oregon green 514 at either the periphery or the core
K.biological_context: Caco-2 cells (human intestinal epithelial cell line)
limitations: In vitro study in a single cell line (Caco-2)
Only one dendrimer generation (G3) tested
Fluorophore conjugation may alter native dendrimer behavior
No quantitative uptake or trafficking rates reported
K.title: Internalization and Subcellular Trafficking of Poly-l-lysine Dendrimers Are Impacted by the Site of Fluorophore Conjugation.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to intracellular uptake, internalization, or endosomal behavior of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: This review confirms that polylysine is efficiently internalized via electrostatic interaction with cells, enabling intracellular delivery, and that modifying contrast agents with polylysine improves cellular uptake. It provides contextual support for intracellular uptake of lysine-based materials.
reported_outcomes: improved cellular uptake of contrast agents
reported_qualitative_findings: polylysine is efficiently internalized via electrostatic interaction with cells
conjugation with functional groups imparts stimuli-responsive traits for enhanced delivery
modifying contrast agents with polylysine increases cellular uptake and stability

limitations: Review article: does not provide primary experimental data on endosomal behavior or detailed uptake mechanisms

K.title: Advanced Delivery Systems Based on Lysine or Lysine Polymers.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to cytotoxicity, biocompatibility, hemolysis, or safety of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: Polylysine-based copolymer PPDD showed no detectable hemolysis or organ toxicity in biosafety assays, was biocompatible, and improved survival and reduced inflammation in sepsis models.
reported_numeric_results: Day-14 survival 80% in PPDD-treated group vs 20% in septic controls
reported_qualitative_findings: No detectable hemolysis or organ toxicity
Biocompatible
PPDD disassembles and reconfigures from spherical to ellipsoidal in acidic environment
K.material_or_molecular_context: Polylysine (PLL)-based copolymer self-assembly (PPDD) composed of PEG-PLL conjugated with DCFH-DA

limitations: Specific cytotoxicity data on normal cells not reported
Safety assessment limited to hemolysis and organ toxicity; other cytotoxicity endpoints not mentioned

K.title: Polylysine-based copolymer self-assemblies featuring acidity-activated structural transformation perceives and relieves sepsis.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to cytotoxicity, biocompatibility, hemolysis, or safety of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: Poly-L-lysine/hyodeoxycholic acid nanoparticles (PLL-HDCA NPs) were evaluated for cytotoxicity, hemolysis, and safety. Cytotoxicity and hemolysis tests showed minimal impact on human cells and significantly reduced hemolysis compared to PLL alone. Skin irritation tests confirmed safety for external application, directly addressing the query's focus on biocompatibility and safety of lysine-based materials.
reported_qualitative_findings: minimal impact on human cells
significantly reduced hemolysis rates compared to PLL alone
confirmed safety for external application
K.biological_context: Human cells (in vitro cytotoxicity and hemolysis), mouse models (in vivo hemorrhage, wound healing, skin irritation)
limitations: Cell types used in cytotoxicity tests not specified

K.title: Computer-Aided Construction and Evaluation of Poly-L-Lysine/Hyodeoxycholic Acid Nanoparticles for Hemorrhage and Infection Therapy.

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to cytotoxicity, biocompatibility, hemolysis, or safety of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: This hydrogel study directly assesses ε-polylysine biocompatibility via hemolysis and cytotoxicity assays, reporting low hemolysis (<5%) and high cell viability (>80%), with in vivo wound healing acceleration.
reported_outcomes: biocompatibility assessment via hemolysis and cytotoxicity assays
in vivo wound healing efficacy in full-thickness skin defect model
reported_numeric_results: 86% wound healing rate within 7 days vs 67% control
reported_qualitative_findings: hydrogel is biocompatible
promotes wound healing by inhibiting inflammatory response
reduces IL-6 levels
enhances angiogenesis
accelerates collagen deposition
does not induce significant inflammatory response in vivo
K.material_or_molecular_context: PGA-PL composite hydrogel: γ-polyglutamic acid (γ-PGA) crosslinked with ε-polylysine (ε-PL) via Schiff base reaction
K.biological_context: in vitro hemolysis assay (blood), in vitro cytotoxicity assay (cell culture), in vivo full-thickness skin defect model in Sprague Dawley rats

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to dendritic-cell activation, antigen presentation, cross-presentation, immune activation, adjuvant activity, or vaccine responses of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: The polyleucine–polylysine conjugate L15K6 enhances antigen uptake by dendritic cells, promotes DC maturation (CD40, CD80/86, MHC-II), upregulates TLR4, activates NF-κB, and induces robust antibody responses when co-delivered with antigens, including outperforming alum. This directly addresses lysine-based polypeptide adjuvant activity and dendritic-cell activation.
reported_outcomes: antibacterial activity against Group A Streptococcus

K.question: What evidence is most relevant to dendritic-cell activation, antigen presentation, cross-presentation, immune activation, adjuvant activity, or vaccine responses of polylysine or lysine-based polypeptide materials?
K.summary: This study demonstrates that chiral polypeptide nanoparticles (P_D-K and P_L-K) composed of poly(L-phenylalanine)-block-poly(lysine) act as nanoadjuvants, with the D-lysine variant P_D-K more potently inducing dendritic cell maturation, antigen cross-presentation, and adaptive immune responses compared to the L-lysine counterpart. The nanovaccine P_D-K-OVA showed high efficacy in preventing and treating B16-OVA melanoma, achieving tumor inhibition rates of up to 94.9% alone and 97.0% with anti-PD-1 therapy.
reported_outcomes: tumor prevention and treatment in B16-OVA melanoma model
reported_numeric_results: tumor inhibition rate of 97.0% when combined with anti-PD-1 antibody
reported_qualitative_findings: Compared to P_L-K-OVA, P_D-K-OVA more robustly induced dendritic cell maturation, antigen cross-presentation, and adaptive immune response.
P_D-K-OVA effectively prevented and treated the OVA-expressed B16-OVA melanoma model.
K.material_or_molecular_context: Chiral polypeptide nanoparticles: poly(L-phenylalanine)-block-poly(L-lysine) (P_L-K) and poly(L-phenylalanine)-block-poly(D-lysine) (P_D-K), self-assembled into nanoparticles mixed with OVA antigen.
K.biological_context: In vitro dendritic cell maturation; in vivo B16-OVA melanoma model in mice; combined with anti-PD-1 antibody.

R.question: What evidence is most relevant to polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials for antigen, protein, vaccine, mRNA, or biomacromolecule delivery?

inhibition of systemic release of pro-inflammatory cytokines

R.question: What evidence is most relevant to polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials for antigen, protein, vaccine, mRNA, or biomacromolecule delivery?
R.summary: Polyarginine (R9) protein transduction domain efficiently delivers protein antigen (OVA) to dendritic cells (DCs), resulting in enhanced MHC class I and II presentation, potent CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell activation, and superior antitumor immunity in a mouse tumor model.

Activation of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells
Complete rejection of tumors with adjuvant co-injection

R.question: What evidence is most relevant to polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials for antigen, protein, vaccine, mRNA, or biomacromolecule delivery?
R.summary: Polyarginine (11R) protein transduction domain enables efficient in vivo delivery of proteins and bioactive compounds across plasma membranes, with subcellular targeting and broad tissue distribution.

in vivo delivery to brain, heart, skeletal muscle, liver, pancreas, lymphocytes
reported_qualitative_findings: very efficient method applicable to cultured cells, tissue slices, and whole animals

R.question: What evidence is most relevant to intracellular uptake, internalization, or endosomal behavior of polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials?
R.summary: Nonaarginine (R9) internalizes into mammalian cells exclusively via endocytosis, requiring binding to cell surface heparan sulfate, with subsequent release from endocytic vesicles. In live cells, R9 is confined to endocytic vesicles, contradicting earlier fixation-artifact claims of cytosolic/nucleolar localization.

demonstrate that PTD internalization occurs via endocytosis rather than direct plasma membrane crossing
reported_numeric_results: K(d) = 109 nM (affinity of R9 for heparin)

R.biological_context: mammalian cells (including heparan sulfate-deficient cells) and liposomes

No direct measurement of endosomal escape efficiency or intracellular trafficking kinetics

R.question: What evidence is most relevant to intracellular uptake, internalization, or endosomal behavior of polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials?
R.summary: This study demonstrates that supercharged arginine-rich peptides (polyarginine analogs of dfTAT) induce late endosome leakage and enhance cytosolic penetration in live human cells. Endocytic uptake efficiency increases linearly with arginine number, while cytosolic penetration shows a threshold effect requiring a minimum number of arginines. Polylysine analogs do not recapitulate this activity, indicating arginine-specific endosomolytic behavior.
reported_qualitative_findings: Leakage activity of dfTAT can be recapitulated by polyarginine analogs but not by polylysine counterparts.
Efficiencies of peptide endocytic uptake increase linearly with the number of arginine residues.
Peptide cytosolic penetration displays a threshold behavior requiring a minimum number of arginines.
Increasing arginine content above threshold augments delivery efficiencies but also increases toxicity.
There is a narrow arginine-content window for optimally active endosomolytic agents.
R.material_or_molecular_context: Supercharged arginine-rich peptides (polyarginine analogs of dfTAT); polylysine counterparts used for comparison
limitations: Study uses specific dfTAT peptide analogs; generalizability to other arginine-based polypeptides may vary.
The exact numerical threshold for arginine number is not specified in the abstract.
Cell type specific effects are not detailed; only 'live human cells' are mentioned.
Toxicity is only qualitatively discussed without specific metrics.
R.title: Unlocking Endosomal Entrapment with Supercharged Arginine-Rich Peptides.

R.question: What evidence is most relevant to intracellular uptake, internalization, or endosomal behavior of polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials?
R.summary: This simulation study shows that polyarginine (R8) peptides penetrate the membrane via a water pore, and conjugation to small nanoparticles with appropriate linker lengths improves translocation efficiency by prolonging water pore lifetime and attracting negative lipids. R.question: What evidence is most relevant to cytotoxicity, biocompatibility, hemolysis, or safety of polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials?
R.summary: Polyarginine coated magnetic nanovectors were evaluated for in vivo safety and compared to PEI-coated ones; pArg coating was found safe and tolerable, while PEI caused severe hemoincompatibility and organ damage.

R.question: What evidence is most relevant to cytotoxicity, biocompatibility, hemolysis, or safety of polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials?
R.summary: This study evaluated safety of poly-arginine-18 (R18 and R18D) in ex vivo models of mast cell degranulation and hemolysis. Neither R18 nor R18D induced significant mast cell degranulation up to 16 µM. R18 caused modest hemolysis at 16 µM only without plasma; R18D caused none. R.question: What evidence is most relevant to cytotoxicity, biocompatibility, hemolysis, or safety of polyarginine or arginine-based polypeptide materials?
R.summary: R15, a synthetic polyarginine peptide (15 arginines), was evaluated for safety in vitro and in vivo as a potential heparin reversal agent. It induced erythrocyte aggregation, thickened fibrin fibers, activated complement, and caused anticoagulation in a concentration-dependent manner, but these effects were mitigated in whole blood or when complexed with heparin. R15 degraded rapidly in rat plasma, was nonimmunogenic, and showed no significant renal dysfunction at therapeutic doses, in contrast to protamine sulfate. The study supports the safety of R15 for heparin reversal but does not directly assess general cytotoxicity or hemolysis.

reported_qualitative_findings: R15 and PS both induce erythrocyte aggregation, thicken fibrin fibers, activate complement, and cause anticoagulation in a concentration-dependent manner

Dramatically enhanced complement activation with excess UFH in UFH-PS complexes, slight increase in UFH-R15 complexes
R15 degraded within 2 h in rat plasma in vitro, whereas PS was not degraded
Enhanced creatinine after single injection of PS or R15 suggests possible abnormal renal function
UFH-PS complex exhibited obvious immunogenicity; UFH-R15 complex did not
R15 is nonimmunogenic and potentially safe at therapeutic dose to reverse UFH effects
R.material_or_molecular_context: R15, a linear synthetic polyarginine peptide composed of 15 L-arginine residues
R.biological_context: In vitro: human erythrocytes, fibrin, complement system, rat plasma. In vivo: rats (intravenous injection), assessment of immunogenicity and renal function.
